small changes that can help you get slimlosing weight can be a challenging task, and many people find it difficult to make significant changes to their diet and lifestyle. however, even small changes can make a big difference when it comes to losing weight and getting slim. here are some small changes that you can make to your daily routine to help you get slim:drink more waterdrinking more water is a simple yet effective way to help you get slim. water helps to keep you hydrated, which can reduce hunger and prevent overeating. additionally, drinking water instead of sugary drinks can help you reduce your calorie intake.get more sleepgetting enough sleep is essential for weight loss and overall health. lack of sleep can disrupt your hormones and increase your appetite, leading to weight gain. aim to get at least seven to eight hours of sleep every night.reduce your portion sizesreducing your portion sizes can help you get slim without having to give up your favorite foods. using smaller plates, bowls, and cups can help you eat smaller portions and reduce your calorie intake.walk morewalking is an easy and low-impact way to get some exercise and help you get slim. aim to walk at least 10,000 steps per day, or try taking the stairs instead of the elevator.eat more proteineating more protein can help you feel full and reduce your calorie intake. incorporate lean proteins such as chicken, fish, and tofu into your meals.choose whole foodschoosing whole, unprocessed foods such as fruits, vegetables, lean proteins, and whole grains can help you get slim and improve your overall health. avoid processed and sugary foods, as they can contribute to weight gain and negatively affect your health. keep a food diarykeeping a food diary can help you identify unhealthy eating patterns and track your progress. write down everything you eat and drink, including portion sizes and calories.limit your alcohol intakelimiting your alcohol intake can help you get slim and improve your overall health. avoid sugary drinks and stick to one to two drinks per day.incorporate high-fiber foodsincorporating high-fiber foods such as beans, whole grains, and vegetables can help you feel full and reduce your calorie intake.find a workout buddyworking out with a friend or family member can help you stay motivated and on track. find a workout buddy and hold each other accountable.in conclusion, incorporating small changes into your daily routine can help you get slim and improve your overall health. by drinking more water, getting more sleep, reducing your portion sizes, walking more, eating more protein, choosing whole foods, keeping a food diary, limiting your alcohol intake, incorporating high-fiber foods, and finding a workout buddy, you can achieve your weight loss goals and maintain a healthy lifestyle.

part three i went digging in the big box of negatives last night and found some date and location clues for these old glass negatives that i have posted and will continue to post. an antique dealer's card was found, from pennsylvania. the card says these photos to circa 1890's. based on the fact that these are all dry plate negatives, that seems reasonable. i started scanning another box of negatives last night and found a political flyer from pottsville, pa. originally we thought these photos were local to ma, but that no longer seems to be the case! so if you or someone you know is from pennsylvania, please share these photos  here are a couple photos scanned in last night, more to follow! if anyone knows of a gab group for old photos that would enjoy these, please let me now! i haven't found any such groups in my search. part twostill working on dates, locations, descriptions for these photos i scanned in 2017. some of the boxes have descriptions on the inside cover of the boxes, but i don't remember which slides came from which boxes, so that is a project that will be tackled when i get back into scanning. these glass negatives already scanned in were the cleanest of the bunch. the rest will require careful extraction from deteriorated boxes covered in bat poo and dust. these are stored in a family member's barn for decades (but are not originated from our family), and the years were not kind. in the meantime, please enjoy   i have 1-2 more batches of these photos before i need to scan more. part 1 - colorized pictures now available in commentssix years ago, some family gave me glass negatives from a barn in brimfield, ma (home of the famous brimfield flea market). i started scanning them in, and then life and babies happened and i never finished. before i start scanning more, i figured the ones already done should see the light of day! so please enjoy these slides, it's a labor of love, with more to come before i get back into it!

"even the prehistoric trukese, however, probably couldn t match the aggression of another group of big-drinking brawlers the pre-modern irish. the victorian-era boyos  fondness for recreational violence was simply mind-boggling. of the 1,932 homicides reported to police between 1866 and 1892, for example, 41 percent were from brawling for fun. at roughly 35 deaths per year (and no doubt countless injuries) this might seem unbelievably high, but for two factors. first, the irish didn t fight bare-handed, but with lethal stick weapons such as the lead-filled, knobbed, blackthorn-wood shillelagh a cross between a walking stick and a long croquet mallet. second, they also didn t fight alone, but in massive gangs, sometimes of hundreds or even thousands, known as factions. these armed hordes might form on the flimsiest of excuses: limerick, for example, was the battleground of the  three-year-olds  and  four-year-olds,  who took opposing sides in a 30-year debate over the age of a calf. equally absurd were the pretexts used to get a stick fight going irish author william carleton describes challengers strutting before opposing factions at county fairs (a frequent venue for faction fights) swinging their shillelaghs and shouting,  ram s horns! who dares say anything s crookeder than ram s horns?  or,  black s the white of my eye. who dares say black s not the white of my eye?  the fact that these were consensual fights, engaged in purely for fun, is shown by the refusal of irish courts to convict those who killed in faction fights only 8 percent ever received prison sentences of more than 2 years."

(complete bio, via historian and researcher based in coeur d'alene, idaho, (formerly of tacoma, washington). specializing in the spanish-colonial history of the pacific northwest, and early maritime / regional history of new england.gavin's research in the field of pacific northwest studies is an extension of the work and findings of donald m. viles, author of "hidden heritage of new spain." mr. viles was one of only a handful of historians and researchers who are responsible for ensuring an entire epoch of north american history was not lost to the ages; chronicling the true colonial expansion of the spanish empire on this continent. viles' work was centered on the "spanish geographical adjustment rule," in which spain intentionally distorted the locations of their north american colonies by 20 degrees of latitude. this was in order to conceal from england, france, and other european rivals the extent of their empire and mining locations in the northern territories of new spain; modern-day washington, oregon, idaho, and british columbia. gavin hopes his findings will do justice to the work of a great northwest historian, and contribute a valuable body of evidence to this occult topic.along with his pacific-northwest research, gavin also specializes in new england maritime and regional history, having spent nearly a combined seven years living in salem & peabody, massachusetts (traveling back and forth from the pnw.) please dm for research requests and academic / press inquiries...

#imageofthedaydickinson crater on venus this november 1996 image from magellan shows dickinson, an impact crater in the northeastern atalanta region of venus. the image is approximately 115 miles (185 kilometers) wide at the base and 43 miles (69 kilometers) in diameter. the crater is complex, characterized by a partial central ring and a floor flooded by radar-dark and radar-bright materials. hummocky, rough-textured ejecta extend all around the crater, except to the west. the lack of ejecta to the west may indicate that the impactor that produced the crater was an oblique impact from the west. extensive radar-bright flows that emanate from the crater's eastern walls may represent large volumes of impact melt, or they may be the result of volcanic material released from the subsurface during the cratering event.magellan was the first planetary spacecraft launched from a space shuttle. now the agency is planning an even more adventurous mission davinci, which will be the first mission to study venus using both spacecraft flybys and a descent probe.image credit: nasa/jpl-caltech hello gab!this account is run by nasa engineers and nasa scientists giving you the latest space news!feel free to ask questions, share our posts and share interesting articles with us! we are happy to communicate with the community!ad astra

baby got back ribs!so i use an electric smoker and applewood wood chips and hickory chips. take a knife and score the back side of the ribs so the membrane will peel off easier when they are done or you can remove all of the membrane. i use a local rib rub that i get at a bbq joint here locally or you can use any recipe you may have. apply the rub and cover the top generously then put some brown sugar on after the rub and let it soak into the ribs. wrap them up and put in the fridge overnight or at least 6 hours if you are pressed for time. fire up the smoker and put temp on 220 degrees they will take 5-7 hrs or until done, you can take a pair of tongs and see if they are tender or until the bones start to show on the sides or if in doubt wrap then in foil and put back on for 1 hr. you want to make sure you are adding more wood chips throughout the smoking process i usually rotate between hickory and applewood chips or you can mix 1/2 and 1/2. i add local raw honey and more rib rub when they are finished and i scrape off the remaining membrane on the bottom layer. enjoy!! chef j dub 420 the smoking okie...........

app.the simplicity of paper walletsgenerating a bitcoin paper wallet is absurdly simple. all that s required is the creation of a random private key and its corresponding public address. this isn t some complex cryptographic challenge that requires advanced engineering it s literally just generating and displaying a set of characters. if we can have a calculator app by default, why not a bitcoin paper wallet generator?the case for a default paper wallet appoperating systems already include basic utilities for essential tasks text editors, calculators, and screenshot tools. a paper wallet generator fits right in. here s why:1. instant self-custody   the main value proposition of bitcoin is financial sovereignty. with a built-in wallet generator, anyone could create a secure, offline bitcoin wallet in seconds, eliminating reliance on third-party apps and websites.2. security & trust   right now, users seeking paper wallets turn to random online generators, many of which could be compromised. a system-integrated tool would offer a trustworthy, open-source solution that s more difficult to tamper with.3. education & adoption   bitcoin adoption suffers from a perceived technical barrier. having an os-level app introduces more people to the idea of self-custody and secure, offline storage.4. developer opportunity   this is low-hanging fruit for developers looking to make an impact. a simple, well-designed, open-source tool could be integrated into linux, windows, and macos, or even as an android/ios utility.the call to actionit s shocking that, over a decade into bitcoin s existence, a standard, offline wallet generator isn t a basic feature on computers. we have notepad, yet no native way to print a bitcoin wallet? developers, open-source contributors, and ambitious students this is your chance to bring a necessary tool to the masses. the best solutions are often the simplest ones. let s make it happen.

*** medal of honor monday!      *** on this day in 1985, a hero passes away. daniel w. lee, sr. made a solo attack on the enemy during world war ii. he survived the experience and received a medal of honor after the war.unfortunately, he lost a battle with liver cancer in 1985. dan was very modest,  his wife told a reporter at the time.  unless specifically asked, he did not elaborate much about [his medal].  many years before, the university of georgia graduate had tried to join the u.s. army air forces, but he was denied because of his colorblindness. he ultimately enlisted in the army in march 1942, just after pearl harbor.the army air forces  loss was the 7th army s gain.lee s heroism came on september 2, 1944, as he served in montreval, france. germans had surrounded the town. for hours, the two sides engaged in a  pitched battle,  as lee s citation would describe.the defenders inside montreval were badly outnumbered, and it wasn t going well, to say the least. finally, lee decided to go after the enemy mortars that were inflicting such heavy damage. he organized a patrol and led them to the edge of town.the group had forced some enemy riflemen out of position on a ridge when lee looked down. seven germans were manning two large mortars about 100 yards away. taking only his rifle and some grenades, he left his men behind and began crawling toward the enemy. he was about 30 yards short of his goal when the enemy noticed him and began firing.his right thigh was shattered. scorning retreat,  his medal citation describes,  bleeding, and suffering intense pain, he dragged himself relentlessly forward. he killed five of the enemy with rifle fire, and the others fled before he reached their position. suddenly, lee found himself under attack by an enemy armored car, and he hastily took cover behind a german half-track (military vehicle) that he d already seen nearby. in a lucky twist, he found a german panzerfaust behind the vehicle. grabbing the rocket launcher, he maneuvered himself into position and blasted the armored car with it. as the car retreated, lee dragged himself back to his men.he'd lost a lot of blood by then, and he collapsed.lee s medal citation doesn t relay what came next: the germans ended up winning the day, and they took many of our soldiers captive. lee was so badly wounded, though, that they left him behind.the decision likely saved lee s life. he survived and received a promotion to first lieutenant. he also received a medal of honor from harry truman. dad was a very humble man,  lee s daughter said in an interview for a university of georgia publication.  he was very much a patriot and a man of faith. we found the bible he carried during the war after he died. he truly believed in our country and his faith got him through all those difficult days. another member of the greatest generation giving his all for love of country. rest in peace, sir.---------------------------gentle reminder: history posts are there's a widely embraced concept known as "defense in depth". it refers to a security approach that layers multiple lines of defense throughout an information system, which can include antivirus software, firewalls, encryption, and more. this methodology can be quite effective in preventing cyber threats from breaching your system. interestingly, this same concept can also be applied to raised bed square foot gardening with similar effectiveness. the raised bed garden: your gardening "firewall"consider your raised bed garden as the initial "firewall" against various threats. in cybersecurity, a firewall is used to prevent unauthorized access to or from a private network. similarly, a raised bed garden can protect your plants from many common threats found at ground level, including certain pests, weeds, and even potential water-logging due to poor soil drainage. just as a firewall scrutinizes network traffic, the raised bed provides a first line of defense against garden intruders.square foot gardening: the "antivirus" of planting techniquessquare foot gardening acts like the antivirus software of the gardening world. in the same way that antivirus software scans your computer to protect it from malware, practicing square foot gardening allows you to keep a close eye on each plant and its immediate neighbors. this practice helps in the early detection of plant disease and pest infestation, enabling you to react quickly and mitigate damage, much like how an antivirus program detects and quarantines a computer virus before it can spread.crop rotation and diversity: "encryption" for soil healthin cybersecurity, encryption helps ensure data integrity and prevents unauthorized access. in square foot gardening, crop rotation and plant diversity are akin to "encrypting" the soil's nutrients. different plants have different nutritional needs and pest/disease profiles. by rotating crops and planting a diverse range of species, you can help prevent any one type of pest or disease from proliferating. similarly, different plants draw on different soil nutrients, helping to ensure that no single nutrient is exhausted (decrypted, if you will).mulching: the "intrusion detection system"mulching in square foot gardening can act as an "intrusion detection system," a component of cybersecurity that monitors a network or systems for malicious activity or policy violations. by adding a layer of mulch to your garden, you are creating a barrier that can help prevent the intrusion of weeds, retain soil moisture, and moderate soil temperature - critical factors for healthy plant growth.companion planting: the "access control" systemjust like an access control system in cybersecurity that restricts the users to access certain information, companion planting in a square foot garden restricts pest access to plants. certain plants can repel specific pests, so when they are planted next to a susceptible plant, pests are less likely to cause damage. this concept can be likened to the cybersecurity principle of granting users the least amount of access necessary for them to perform their tasks.the principles of defense in depth from cybersecurity provide a compelling framework for managing a raised bed square foot garden. it's a gardening strategy that offers a layered defense against a wide range of threats, improves efficiency, and promotes a healthier and more productive garden. so, the next time you're planning or tending to your garden, remember these principles and consider how a cybersecurity mindset could make you a more successful gardener.thanks for playing along :)
